description: Replace the DMS-983 terminal-stage seam with an executor-facing write request for DMS-984. Acceptance: `RelationalDocumentStoreRepository` selects the active `MappingSet`, `ResourceWritePlan`, and, for existing-document flows, the `ResourceReadPlan`, then hands one executor request into a new relational write executor service instead of calling a terminal stage directly. Introduce executor-facing contracts that carry the selected body, operation kind, target lookup result, mapping-set-scoped plans, trace metadata, and any executor-only diagnostics without forcing later runtime stages to rediscover them. `FlatteningInput`, `FlattenedWriteSet`, and the candidate row-buffer contracts remain usable by the executor, but `IRelationalWriteTerminalStage` is removed or demoted so it is no longer the architectural boundary for persistence orchestration.
steps-to-verify: Add backend unit tests that prove the repository still enforces write-plan and read-plan guard rails, shapes the new executor request correctly, and no longer depends on `IRelationalWriteTerminalStage`.

description: Replace the temporary PUT target-resolution seam with operation-correct lookup semantics. Acceptance: POST lookup returns either `CreateNew` or `ExistingDocument`; PUT lookup returns either `ExistingDocument` or `NotFound`; existing-document lookup includes `DocumentId`, `DocumentUuid`, and the observed `ContentVersion`; `RelationalWriteTargetContext` remains executor-facing and only models real write targets (`CreateNew` or `ExistingDocument`); `UpdateDocumentById` short-circuits missing PUT targets to `UpdateFailureNotExists` before reference resolution, flattening, current-state load, or executor execution; legacy behavior that converted missing PUT targets into `CreateNew` is removed from both production code and tests.
steps-to-verify: Add unit tests for POST create-vs-update lookup, PUT existing-vs-not-found lookup, and repository short-circuit mapping to `UpdateFailureNotExists`.

description: Introduce a request-scoped relational write session that owns one open connection and transaction per executor attempt. Acceptance: the write executor can use a shared connection and transaction for prerequisite lookups, current-state hydration, `CollectionItemId` reservation, and final DML on both PostgreSQL and SQL Server; commit and rollback are explicit and attempt-scoped; the old one-command-one-connection pattern no longer dictates write orchestration; low-level command executors may remain as utilities, but orchestration no longer depends on them as the primary seam; the session seam leaves room for future authorization statements to be prepended into the same roundtrip without another boundary redesign.
steps-to-verify: Add backend unit tests for session lifecycle, commit and rollback behavior, and dialect selection for executor attempts.

description: Move request-scoped reference resolution under the write executor so it can share the executor-owned session. Acceptance: the executor resolves document and descriptor references through the shared session without opening independent connections, preserves existing request-local memoization and reference-failure classification semantics, and short-circuits before flattening or DML when reference resolution fails. Reference failures continue to map to the current public `UpsertFailureReference` and `UpdateFailureReference` results.
steps-to-verify: Add backend unit tests that prove the executor resolves references through the shared attempt boundary, preserves memoization behavior, and exits before flattening or DML on reference failures.

description: Move flattener invocation under the write executor after reference resolution succeeds. Acceptance: the repository no longer constructs `FlatteningInput` or `FlattenedWriteSet`; the executor builds `FlatteningInput` from the selected request body, resolved references, and executor-facing target context; the flattener contract remains pure request-body to row-buffer transformation with no session ownership; validation failures still short-circuit before any DML and continue to map to the current public validation results.
steps-to-verify: Add backend unit tests that prove the executor constructs `FlatteningInput` only after successful reference resolution and that repository-level result mapping stays unchanged for flattener validation failures.

description: Add a write-path-local, session-aware current-state loader for one existing document using the compiled read plan and `HydrationExecutor`. Acceptance: DMS-984 can load `DocumentMetadataRow` plus hydrated table rows for a single `DocumentId` through the executor-owned connection and transaction using `PageKeysetSpec.Single`; the loader is narrow and rowset-first, with no profile projection or JSON reconstitution requirements; public `IDocumentHydrator` stays unchanged for the read path; existing-document write attempts fail deterministically when a required `ResourceReadPlan` is missing; the loaded current state is reusable by both guarded no-op comparison and later DMS-1105 work; tests prove the guarded no-op path reuses this same current-state load rather than issuing a dedicated extra compare-only roundtrip.
steps-to-verify: Add backend or plans tests that prove an existing-document write attempt can materialize current metadata plus table rows from the selected read plan without opening a second connection seam, and that guarded no-op preparation reuses this load instead of performing a second compare-only load.

description: Implement the shared no-profile post-merge rowset synthesis helper for existing-document writes. Acceptance: PUT and POST-as-update use one shared helper for merge matching, deterministic sibling ordering, compare projection, and execution-ready rowset synthesis rather than separate compare-only logic; synthesis consumes `CollectionMergePlan.CompareBindingIndexesInOrder` and the same stable-identity metadata used by the real executor; the helper can project both non-collection scopes and collection scopes into the same stored and writable comparison space that later DML execution will use.
steps-to-verify: Add backend and plans unit tests for compare-order reuse, deterministic sibling ordering, and shared rowset synthesis for non-collection and collection paths.

description: Enforce the DMS-984 identity-stable boundary for existing-document writes. Acceptance: existing-document writes only proceed when the post-merge identity projection matches the stored identity projection; `allowIdentityUpdates=false` yields the normal immutable-identity failure path; resources that may eventually allow identity updates yield a deterministic relational not-yet-supported failure until the E09 identity-maintenance stories land; identity-changing cases are rejected before changed-write DML or guarded no-op success is returned.
steps-to-verify: Add backend unit tests for identity-stable success, immutable-identity failure for `allowIdentityUpdates=false`, and deterministic not-yet-supported failure for `allowIdentityUpdates=true`.

description: Introduce internal executor attempt outcomes and implement the guarded no-op fast path for unchanged existing-document writes. Acceptance: the executor returns internal attempt results such as applied write, guarded no-op, and stale no-op compare rather than only public `UpsertResult` and `UpdateResult`; unchanged PUT and unchanged POST-as-update requests short-circuit as successful no-ops without issuing DML or bumping `dms.Document.ContentVersion`; the compare path reuses the same shared post-merge synthesis logic as execution; before returning success, the executor revalidates that the observed `ContentVersion` is still current for the target document; stale compares surface an internal stale outcome instead of returning success from stale state.
steps-to-verify: Add backend unit tests for internal attempt outcome mapping, unchanged PUT, unchanged POST-as-update, no-DML short-circuiting, and stale compare classification after freshness recheck.

description: Implement repository-level stale-no-op retry handling on top of the executor's internal attempt outcomes. Acceptance: the repository maps successful attempts back to `InsertSuccess`, `UpdateSuccess`, or successful PUT responses; when a no-op compare goes stale and there is no external `If-Match` policy yet, the repository reruns exactly one full executor attempt against fresh state; if the retry also goes stale, the request maps to a write-conflict outcome rather than returning success from stale state; database exception classification and general retry-loop policy remain out of scope for this task.
steps-to-verify: Add backend unit tests for stale-no-op classification, one-time retry behavior, and result mapping back to public repository outcomes.

description: Implement transactional DML for `dms.Document`, the resource root row, root extension rows, and non-collection separate-table or inlined scopes on the no-profile path. Acceptance: create flows insert `dms.Document` and the required relational rows in dependency order; update flows update matched rows, insert newly present separate-table rows, delete omitted separate-table rows, and clear compiled bindings for omitted inlined scopes instead of preserving hidden data; no-profile root `_ext` rows and aligned one-to-one extension scopes follow the same present and absent semantics as base data; the executor commits all changed rows in one transaction and rolls back fully on failure with no partial writes left behind.
steps-to-verify: Add backend unit tests for non-collection present and absent handling, inlined clear behavior, root extension row handling, and rollback-on-failure behavior using an injected failure hook.

description: Implement stable-identity merge execution for base collection and common-type tables on the no-profile path. Acceptance: the executor loads the current sibling set from the current-state loader, matches request candidates to stored rows by compiled semantic identity, updates matched rows in place, deletes omitted rows by stable row identity, reserves new `CollectionItemId` values only for unmatched inserts, and applies the same logic to both top-level and nested collection scopes. `Ordinal` recomputation uses the same deterministic post-merge ordering helper used by the guarded no-op compare path. `FullSurfaceCollectionReorder` at base collection scopes must prove matched rows keep their existing `CollectionItemId` values while only `Ordinal` changes.
steps-to-verify: Add backend and plans unit tests for semantic-identity matching, matched-row preservation, delete-plus-insert on semantic identity changes, nested collection handling, and ordinal recomputation.

description: Extend stable-identity merge execution to no-profile extension child collections. Acceptance: root-level extension child collections and collection-aligned extension child collections use the same semantic-identity matching, matched-row preservation, delete, insert, `CollectionItemId` reservation, and ordinal recomputation rules as base collections; collection-aligned extension child collections remain keyed to the owning base row's stable identity rather than request ordinals; executor-side merge helpers stay shared instead of forking an extension-only implementation.
steps-to-verify: Add backend and plans unit tests for root-level extension child collections, collection-aligned extension child collections, and stable ordering and identity preservation across those scopes.

description: Implement batched relational DML that respects dialect-specific parameter limits without introducing provider-specific bulk-loader paths in this story. Acceptance: inserts and updates are grouped to avoid N+1 execution patterns; multi-row insert chunking and parameter partitioning honor PostgreSQL and SQL Server parameter limits; update execution proves changed rows are applied through bounded grouped commands rather than one command per row; `CollectionItemId` reservation is batched by table or scope as needed; large collections that exceed one batch are persisted through multiple bounded batches inside the same transaction; provider-specific `COPY` and `SqlBulkCopy` optimizations remain out of scope for DMS-984.
steps-to-verify: Add backend unit tests for batch partitioning decisions, parameter-limit handling, multi-batch collection insert behavior, and update-side batching or command-count behavior that would catch a per-row update fallback.

description: Add the smaller SQL Server safety net this story needs without full SQL Server end-to-end integration. Acceptance: unit or contract tests cover SQL Server generated SQL shape, compare-order metadata consumption, batching and parameter partitioning behavior, and any dialect-specific `CollectionItemId` reservation assumptions touched by DMS-984; PostgreSQL remains the deep end-to-end gate for runtime behavior in this story.
steps-to-verify: Add backend and plans unit or contract tests that exercise the DMS-984 SQL Server-specific SQL and batching paths.

description: Add PostgreSQL integration coverage for the create half of the DMS-984 no-profile runtime baseline using compiled schema and plan fixtures rather than hand-written table definitions. Acceptance: integration tests cover `NoProfileWriteBehavior` POST create with nested collections, root `_ext`, collection `_ext`, and an extension child collection. Assertions are database-first and verify inserted rows, collection identities, extension persistence, and stored values after the write using at least one focused stable-key fixture.
steps-to-verify: Add PostgreSQL integration tests that provision the compiled relational model, execute create flows through the repository and executor, and assert directly against database state for nested and `_ext` create scenarios.

description: Add PostgreSQL integration coverage for the changed-update half of the DMS-984 no-profile runtime baseline. Acceptance: integration tests cover `NoProfileWriteBehavior` PUT update with one omitted separate-table scope and one omitted inlined scope proving delete-vs-clear semantics. Assertions are database-first and verify actual rows, present-vs-absent behavior, and stored values after update using a focused stable-key fixture.
steps-to-verify: Add PostgreSQL integration tests that execute changed PUT flows through the repository and executor and assert directly against database state for omitted separate-table and omitted inlined-scope cases.

category: PostgreSQL Integration - Post-As-Update And Authoritative Smoke
description: Add PostgreSQL integration coverage for POST-as-update on an existing document and a production-like compiled resource shape. Acceptance: integration tests cover `NoProfileWriteBehavior` POST-as-update on an existing document and include one authoritative DS 5.2 or extension-style smoke in addition to the focused fixtures already used elsewhere. Assertions are database-first and verify the public result type plus stored relational state after the write.
steps-to-verify: Add PostgreSQL integration tests that execute POST-as-update flows through the repository and executor and assert directly against database state, including one authoritative production-like fixture smoke.

description: Add PostgreSQL integration coverage for guarded no-op success. Acceptance: integration tests cover unchanged PUT guarded no-op and unchanged POST-as-update guarded no-op; unchanged writes prove unchanged rowsets and unchanged `dms.Document.ContentVersion`. Assertions remain database-first and verify both the public result type and the stored relational state.
steps-to-verify: Add PostgreSQL integration tests that execute unchanged-write scenarios through the repository and executor and assert directly against row contents and `ContentVersion` behavior.

description: Add PostgreSQL integration coverage for `FullSurfaceCollectionReorder`. Acceptance: integration tests prove matched rows keep the same `CollectionItemId` values while only `Ordinal` changes under a no-profile full-surface reorder. Assertions are database-first and verify both the public result type and the stored relational state.
steps-to-verify: Add PostgreSQL integration tests that execute full-surface reorder scenarios through the repository and executor and assert directly against `CollectionItemId` reuse, `Ordinal` values, and stored row contents.

description: Add PostgreSQL integration coverage for stale compare handling. Acceptance: integration tests cover stale compare recheck with a concurrent content-version bump between compare and guarded short-circuit and prove stale no-op does not return success from stale state.
steps-to-verify: Add PostgreSQL integration tests that execute stale-compare scenarios through the repository and executor and assert directly against final database state and public result mapping.

description: Add PostgreSQL integration coverage for multi-batch writes. Acceptance: integration tests cover batch-threshold crossing with a collection large enough to require multiple bounded insert batches inside one transaction and prove the full collection persists correctly across batches.
steps-to-verify: Add PostgreSQL integration tests that execute large-collection scenarios through the repository and executor and assert directly against stored collection rows after multi-batch persistence.

description: Add PostgreSQL integration coverage for transaction rollback. Acceptance: integration tests verify no partial rows commit when an injected failure occurs after an early write inside the executor transaction. Assertions are database-first and prove failed attempts leave no partial relational state behind.
steps-to-verify: Add PostgreSQL integration tests that execute injected-failure scenarios through the repository and executor and assert directly against final database state after rollback.
